newsitem.title: USA: Talbots sees some sales shifting to Oct.
newsitem.headline: Talbots sees some sales shifting to Oct.

text.p: Talbots Inc said Thursday some of its mid-season sales would be shifted to October from September because it plans to move its mid-fall sale by one week.

"As we did with our semiannual sale event this past summer, our upcoming mid-fall sale will also be shifted one week later this year," said Arnold Zetcher, president and chief executive officer. "We continue to believe this makes good business sense, as the timing better matches our customer's shopping patterns. The effect of this change will shift some mid-season sales from September to October."
Earlier Thursday Talbots reported that same store sales increased 3.9 percent in August.

The company said its "catalog sales continued to track to plan" throughout August. "However, we are remaining cautious, as our stores have only been fully converted to fall merchandise for two weeks," Zetcher said.
The company said previously it expects to have a clearer idea on fall trends with September sales.

"We are pleased with our sales performance in August, although the month has become an increasingly smaller part of the fall selling season as customers continue to shop closer to need," Zetcher said.
